title: BitMatrix::transpose 64x64 bit-block + AVX2
description:
## Current

`BitMatrix::transpose` at `crates/gf2-core/src/matrix.rs:858-870` is a naive O(n²) bit-by-bit double loop. No SIMD.

## Fix

Add a new `transpose_fn` to the `LogicalFns` set (or a sibling `TransposeFns` registered via `simd::maybe_transpose()`):

- Scalar fallback: 64×64 bit-block transpose via Hacker's Delight ch. 7.3 (recursive bit-twiddle, ~7 stages of mask + shift + XOR).
- AVX2 SIMD: PSHUFB-based 8×8 byte tiles within YMM, then assemble 64×64 from 4 quadrants.
- V7 cache layout: for `n > 8K`, drive a tiled outer loop that fits L1.

## PPC steps

V0 baseline (add `transpose` bench targeting n ∈ {64, 256, 1024, 4096}) → V4 register tile + bit-twiddle (Hacker's Delight) → V3 SIMD via PSHUFB → V7 cache layout for large n. Target ≥10× on n=4096; pass below this implies trying a different transform (e.g., explicit `_mm256_permute2x128_si256` schedule).

## Per-kernel execution protocol (epic spec doc, all required)

1. Baseline saved (transpose bench is new — saved as part of this task before any other edit).
2. ASM artefacts for the bit-twiddle and PSHUFB paths.
3. `perf stat -r 10` before/after.
4. Proptest equivalence helper from I4: `transpose(transpose(M)) == M`, `transpose(M) * v == v.T * M`-equivalent.
5. Word-boundary `#[test]`s at n ∈ {0, 1, 63, 64, 65, 127, 128, 129}.
6. ≥10× target; if PSHUFB path doesn't reach 10×, document why (cache-bound? bench too small?) and either tune V7 layout or revert.
7. One commit per spiral step (V4-tile / V3-SIMD / V7-layout).

## Depends on

I1, I2, I3, I4.

## Success criteria

- [hard] All proptest invariants hold; word-boundary cases pass.
- [hard] No `unsafe` outside `gf2-kernels-simd`.
- [hard] Transpose bench committed and pinned.
- [aspirational] ≥10× over baseline at n=4096.
